chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Thawrī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the muwaddiḥah wound on the head—whether it is as it is on the face. He said: “The muwaddiḥah and the shijaj wounds on the head and the face are equal in the indemnity, because the face is part of the head; and wounds on the body are not like those on the head.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: financial indemnity paid for bodily injury
key_terms.الرَّأْسِ: the head, as a legal category for injury rulings
key_terms.الشِّجَاجُ: head or face wounds of specified legal categories
key_terms.الْجَسَدِ: the body apart from the head category in this ruling
key_terms.الْمُوضِحَةِ: a wound that exposes the bone
key_terms.الْوَجْهِ: the face, treated here as part of the head in diyah

ai.seo_question: Are head and face wounds treated equally in diyah in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning indemnity for wounds to the head and face. It states that muwaddiḥah and shijaj wounds in the head and face carry the same diyah because the face is considered part of the head, unlike wounds on the rest of the body.
